the La2O 3-malonic acid-modified LiCoV04 material is the best choice as cathode material for lithium-ion cells.

the 0,5 wt % LaO3-coated 60 wt % LiCoVO4/malonic acid cathode material has the most desirable properties, including the best cell performance and thermal stability, among all of the synthesized materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the composite cathode material with 0.5 % La2O 3 and 60 % malonic acid coating exhibited the best electrochemical properties, and the best thermal stability with lower thermal decomposition heat and higher onset temperature of decomposition.

the surface-modified Li1.2Co1.2VO4 cathode materials with La2O 3 and/or malonate showed improved thermal stability, and the best electrochemical performance was obtained for the composite material with 0.5% La2O3, 60 wt % of malonic acid, and calcined at 800 K for 3 h.
the composite material of 0.5% La2O3 coated LiCoVO4 calcined with 30 wt % malonic acids showed the best cell performance and thermal stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
La2O3 surface coating and malonic acid modification are effective methods to enhance the electrochemical performance of LiCoVO 4 cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries.
the surface-modification of LiCoVO 4 with La2 O3 and/or malonate is a viable strategy for enhancing its performance as cathode material for Li-ion cells.
the La2O 3-coated and malonic acid-treated LiCoVO4 composite material can be used as an effective cathode material for Li-ion cells.
